**Evaluating top picks**

I need to find an answer, but I can't definitively say what is the "best." Instead, I’ll think of some top picks. It might be useful to check BBB for information or ratings related to what I'm looking for. This way, I can gather some insights and ensure I'm providing helpful suggestions without claiming any single option stands out as the absolute best.

If you’re looking for the **best restoration company in Federal Way, WA**, my top short-list would be:

## Best overall local pick: **National Restoration Construction**
They look like a strong choice because they serve Federal Way directly, offer **24/7 water, fire, mold, storm, biohazard, and reconstruction services**, and have been operating in the Seattle–Tacoma/South Sound area since **2004**. They also list a WA contractor license and say they can handle both mitigation and rebuild work, which is helpful if damage goes beyond drying/cleanup. ([narestco.com](https://narestco.com/?utm_source=openai))

## Also worth calling: **911 Restoration WA Inc**
911 Restoration WA Inc has a Federal Way BBB profile and offers **water damage restoration, mold remediation, crawl space repairs, and fire/smoke restoration**. I’d consider them a credible comparison call, especially for emergency water or mold work. ([bbb.org](https://www.bbb.org/us/wa/federal-way/profile/restoration-companies/911-restoration-wa-inc-1296-1000194744?utm_source=openai))

## For water-damage-specific comparison: **Pro-Steam**
Expertise.com’s current Federal Way list includes Pro-Steam as a **24/7 carpet cleaning and emergency restoration company** providing water damage services in the area. ([expertise.com](https://www.expertise.com/home-improvement/water-damage/washington/federal-way?utm_source=openai))

### My recommendation
Call **National Restoration Construction first**, then get a second quote from **911 Restoration WA Inc**. For water damage, speed matters, but don’t skip basics: ask for proof of insurance, WA contractor license, IICRC certification, written scope, moisture readings, and whether they bill insurance directly.

If this is an active leak/flood, stop the water source, document photos/video, call your insurance carrier, and get mitigation started ASAP.
